findings.description: In submodule-mount mode (detected solely by `.loa/.claude` being a directory) any manifest path that is absent from the working tree but present under `.loa/<path>` is now counted as informational "not-mounted" instead of failing as Missing. Deleting a mounted security control (e.g. a hook or gate script symlink under `.claude/hooks/` or `.claude/scripts/`) therefore no longer trips the integrity check. The function also now unconditionally `return 0`s, so any caller or `set -e` path that relied on the previous non-zero status when drift was detected will no longer abort.
findings.failure_mode: An attacker (or a prompt-injected agent with shell) removes a mounted enforcement script's symlink; check-loa.sh reports a clean integrity result plus a harmless not-mounted count, and the missing control goes unnoticed.
findings.suggested_fix: Make not-mounted only acceptable for paths explicitly declared optional in the manifest (or a mount-scope allowlist) rather than any path present upstream; keep hooks/, scripts/, rules/ as hard-required. Preserve a non-zero return (or a global failure flag the caller checks) when drift is true instead of `return 0`.

findings.description: The System Zone file-count check now counts `git ls-files -- .claude`, i.e. only tracked files. Previously `find` counted every file on disk. Untracked files planted under `.claude/` (a dropped hook, a new skill, a modified-then-copied script) no longer change ACTUAL_COUNT and so never trigger the mismatch warning. The check also silently falls back to the legacy find count only when the git count is exactly zero, so a tree with any tracked `.claude/` file hides all untracked additions.
findings.failure_mode: Malicious or accidental untracked files added to `.claude/` pass preflight without the integrity warning that previously fired.
findings.suggested_fix: Count tracked files for the manifest comparison but additionally run `git -C "$MANIFEST_TREE" ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- .claude` (minus overrides/) and warn or fail when it is non-empty. Better: replace the count heuristic with the per-file sha256 check that check-loa.sh already performs.

findings.description: The row's `voices_run`, `degraded` and `degraded_reason` fields are derived from `sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-{review,audit}.json`, which lives in the sandbox the evaluated agent writes to. The header explicitly refuses to take `arm` from sandbox/ (DEC-0413) for this reason, but the same trust boundary is crossed for quality metrics: an implement-phase agent can pre-write or edit an envelope with `verdict_quality.status: OK` and inflated `voices_succeeded`, and if the review/audit phase does not overwrite it the row reports a healthy, non-degraded run.
findings.failure_mode: The subject under evaluation can shape its own eval-row quality fields, hiding degraded or incomplete dissent gates and biasing ablation results.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the review/audit phases copy their envelopes into `<run-dir>/eval/` (harness-owned) and read only from there, mirroring the existing `eval/` fallback; or verify the sandbox envelope against a hash recorded by the phase driver in meta/pipeline.json before trusting it.

findings.description: `zone_violations.dot_claude_writes` only inspects Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit tool inputs whose `file_path` matches `(^|/)\.claude/`. Writes performed via the Bash tool (redirects, `cp`, `sed -i`, `ln -s`), writes through a symlink the agent created elsewhere, or paths that normalise into `.claude/` only after resolution are not detected. The row will report zero zone violations for runs that did modify the System Zone.
findings.failure_mode: Ablation metrics under-report System Zone writes, so arms that violate zone rules through the shell appear compliant.
findings.suggested_fix: Also diff the sandbox `.claude/` tree against the pre-run snapshot (hash or `git status --porcelain -- .claude`) at row-build time and report any change as a violation, independent of which tool produced it. Normalise paths (realpath relative to the sandbox) before matching.

findings.description: When `bats` is not on PATH the script executes a hardcoded operator-specific path under `$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats`. This bakes one developer's filesystem layout into a shared harness and will execute whatever binary sits at that path on any other host, with no integrity check.
findings.failure_mode: On a different machine the fingerprint silently incorporates (or executes) an unexpected binary at that path; on the original host anything writable there runs under the operator's account during every fingerprint call.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the hardcoded fallback; require `--bats-bin`/`LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN` or report `bats=absent`.

findings.description: The new `gpt-6.1-sol` entry carries copied gpt-5.5 placeholder prices and a fallback chain to `openai:codex-headless`, whose `cli_model` is now `gpt-6.1-sol` itself. Any spend cap or ledger that relies on estimated cost for this model (MODELINV rows, `cost_usd` in runs.jsonl) is computed from an unconfirmed rate card, and an HTTP failure on the API key automatically re-routes the same model onto the operator's ChatGPT subscription via the CLI hop, where cost is only estimated. If `codex-headless` ever gains a fallback back to an OpenAI primary, this forms a dispatch cycle.
findings.failure_mode: Under-estimated costs let batch runs exceed intended spend limits; API entitlement failures silently shift metered usage onto a personal subscription.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the entry `pricing_confirmed: false` (or similar) and have spend.sh treat unconfirmed pricing conservatively or refuse hard caps on it; confirm the rate card before the sprint close as the comment promises, and add a loop guard test for fallback chains that pass through a CLI hop whose cli_model points back into the chain.
